property_summary: The supportsInterface function must return true for the IAccessControl interface ID; the buggy version always returns false, violating this rule for that specific input.
supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC165).interfaceId; the bug returns false for this input, violating ERC165 introspection consistency.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, if the reference contract's supportsInterface returns true, the mutant must also return true (and vice versa), but the mutant always returns false, violating this equivalence for interfaceIds that the reference accepts.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must not return true when called on the contract itself as msg.sender; the buggy version always returns false, but the correct version returns true for certain interfaceIds even when the caller is the contract, violating the rule that self-calls should be introspectable.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when the caller has the TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE; the buggy version always returns false, violating this for admins calling with type(IAccessControl).interfaceId.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface returns true if and only if interfaceId is type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId in the reference, but the mutant incorrectly returns true only for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, failing for type(IERC165).interfaceId and returning false for all others.

supportInterface must return true for exactly the OR of type(IAccessControl).interfaceId and type(IERC165).interfaceId (inherited from ERC165); the buggy version returns false for type(IERC165).interfaceId when type(IAccessControl).interfaceId is not supported.

For any bytes4 interface identifier, the reference contract's supportsInterface must return the logical OR of type(IAccessControl).interfaceId and type(IERC165).interfaceId, while the buggy version fails to return true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId when passed alone.
For any bytes4 `iface`, the reference contract's `supportsInterface` always returns `true` when `iface` equals `type(IERC165).interfaceId`, but the buggy version returns `false` for that same input.

For any bytes4 `iface`, the reference C returns true for `supportsInterface` when `iface` is `type(IAccessControl).interfaceId` or `type(IERC165).interfaceId` and false otherwise; the mutant returns false for `type(IERC165).interfaceId` when `iface` is `type(IERC165).interfaceId`, breaking the rule that `supportsInterface(type(IERC165).interfaceId)` must return true because ERC165 base contract always returns true for its own interface.

The reference C supports the IERC165 interface in addition to IAccessControl, so supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant removes this inheritance check and returns false for that interfaceId.

For any interface ID, the reference 'supportsInterface' returns true if the ID is type(IERC165).interfaceId (which it always is for this contract). The mutant breaks this by returning false for that ID.

For any interface ID, the reference `supportsInterface` returns `interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId || interfaceId == type(IERC165).interfaceId`, while the mutant returns false for `type(IERC165).interfaceId`.

For any interfaceId, the reference contract's supportsInterface returns true for type(IERC165).interfaceId because it inherits ERC165, but the mutant returns false for that interfaceId since it removes the super call.
For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant breaks this by removing the super call and returning false.
For any role and any account, P.hasRole returns true exactly when the account is a member of the role, while M.hasRole always returns true, violating faithfulness to stored membership.

For any role and account, hasRole must return true if and only if the role has been granted to that account. The bug always returns false, so after granting a role, hasRole should return true in the reference, but returns false in the mutant.
For any role and account, hasRole must never revert, and after granting a role to an account and then renouncing it, hasRole must return false in both the reference and the mutant.

For any role, account, and sender granted the admin role of that role, calling hasRole(role, account) must accurately reflect whether the sender has granted the role to the account; the bug always returns false.

For any role and account, hasRole must return the same boolean as the corresponding internal membership storage, which is true exactly if the role has been granted (and not revoked) to the account; the mutant always returns false regardless of grants.

For any role and account, if the role was granted to the account and the account itself renounces it, hasRole must return false, but after renouncing, re-granting the role to the same account must make hasRole return true again; the buggy version incorrectly returns false after the re-grant.

For any role and account, hasRole must return the exact negation of the buggy version; the reference always returns the actual stored membership while the bug returns the opposite, breaking the invariant that a role explicitly granted via _grantRole returns true.
For a freshly granted role, hasRole on the granting address must return true, but the bug returns false.

For every role and account, hasRole's result must be stable under a double-check: calling it twice in a row must return the same value; the reference satisfies this for all inputs, but the buggy version returns the opposite value, so a caller reading twice could see a flip, violating stability.

For any role and account, the boolean result of 'hasRole' must be consistent with the actual membership stored by the contract; the buggy version negates this, causing a freshly granted role to appear as false when it should be true after a non-self-revoking grant.

For any role and account, hasRole must return true if and only if the role has been granted to that account and not revoked; the buggy version returns the opposite of the stored membership, breaking this correspondence.
For any role, getRoleAdmin should return the admin role previously set, but the mutant returns a fixed hash regardless of the role's actual admin.
For any timelock-admin-configured role, getRoleAdmin returns the admin role set via _setRoleAdmin; the mutant breaks this by returning a hardcoded value regardless of the configured admin.
